newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end mixed to higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended mixed to higher Tuesday, but market sources said no move by the Federal Reserve on interest rates should heighten handwringing over economic data and keep munis rangebound until after the November election.
Municipals ended anywhere from mixed to up 3/8 of a point, players said.

"No Fed puts everything on hold and now you've got to watch the economic numbers coming out," one trader said, adding that employment data as well and producer price index and consumer price index data will be closely watched.

"It probably delays whatever is going to happen until after the election," the trader said. "I think unfortunately we are going to get into this trading range type of mentality and the flow, which has been really difficult over the last couple of weeks, is just going to be more of the same."

Even if the Fed tightened by 25 basis points, the market would likely be similar straits, he said. The trader said while he believed the Fed would leave rates untouched because of the election, a 50 basis point tightening might have jumpstarted the municipal market.

"The best thing today from a business standpoint would have been to do it 50, get the market to drop like a rock and get back to levels where people can do business," he said. "Right now there is no incentive to do anything."

The calendar remains light, bond funds lack cash and the stock market is "sort of hanging around its highs," the trader said. After a malaise-bound summer, players thought activity would pickup after Labor Day but that failed to happen, the trader said.
A municipal analyst said the Fed's decision to stand pat was "a healthly thing."

"I don't think if you really thought about it that anybody would really wish for a 50 basis point change," he said. "I think (the Fed is) anxious to go, but it's too close to call and they've got an election coming up. And though they are not political, if they did this and something happened, one or the other losing party would certainly be all over them in the future."

The analyst said munis overall ended the day up 1/4 to 3/8. Dollar bonds opened flat, added 1/8 point by noon and rose another 1/8 point after the Fed's announcement to end 1/4 point higher. High-grade issues improved by two basis points.

In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed at 113-20/32, while the December T-bond contract closed at 108-20/32. The MOB spread was 160 ticks. In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 14/32 at 97-1/32 to yield 6.99 percent.
Turning to Wednesday's negotiated action, 24 deals totaling $925 million are expected. A $144 million Port of Portland, Oregon, offering via Goldman Sachs & Co, heads the list.
It is subject to the alternative minimum tax.

Also Wednesday, North Central Texas Health Facilities Corp is expected to sell $108 million bonds through Merrill Lynch & Co, while Los Angeles Unified School District, Calif., is scheduled to sell $94 million bonds via Bear Stearns & Co.
On the competitive side, eight sales are scheduled totaling $84.7 million.
Two Pittsburgh School District, Pa., deals, one at $32.4 million and the other at $15.7 million, are scheduled for 1100 EDT Wednesday.
